utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. Good morning to you, sir. May I remind you the affirmation you made at the beginning of your evidence still applies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Stojanovski. You remember, Mr. Stojanovski, that you stated yesterday that you went to Cair for the first time on the 14th of August.

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So, if someone were to assert before this Court that you came to Cair on the evening of Sunday, 12th of August, what would you say to such assertion?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That it is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When I asked you, you also stated that it was the duty of the OVR Cair to file a criminal report on an event. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, OVR Cair.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. I would like to ask you to look now, to find in the larger binder, the document 113 -- in tab 113.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is 65 ter 1D1170. Tab 113.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is a document, as you can see, in the upper corner, coming from the sector for -- of internal affairs of the city of Skopje, department of analytics, Cair.

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And it is an information on the crime of terrorism that is for the preparation to perpetrate terrorists activities, and it involves ten individuals from the Ljuboten village, Skopje region. The first paragraph reads: "The department for internal affairs Cair, today, on 14 August 2001, filed a criminal report to the basic public prosecutor's office, Skopje, for further processing of persons," and then the names of persons who will be handed over are indicated. Tell me, Mr. Stojanovski, does this information corroborate the notion that the OVR Cair was in charge of filing of a criminal report and handing the persons over to the court.

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in view of the fact where this act was committed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: We discussed this issue several times, and you spoke about the duties of the police after it files a criminal report. Tell me, once again, please, what are the obligations of the police once the criminal report has been filed or after it had informed the prosecutor or the investigating judge?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They're no obligations, but we do have a duty in the case that they request of us to undertake certain measures or activities to carry out their request.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski, you stated, yesterday, that you were informed by the persons that you tasked with activities, that you informed them about the room that should have been made available to the detained persons, the duration of their detention, and also the number of criminal reports. Do you remember having testified about this?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were you, at any moment, Mr. Stojanovski, informed of some problems, especially health problems, in some of the detainees?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I received information that one of the persons that were previously brought in the police station Mirkovci was taken to a hospital where this person died.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. Stojanovski, considering the information that one individual was taken to hospital and died there, to whom did the obligation to undertake measures belong and are you aware whether such measures were undertaken?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said previously, in view of the place where this criminal -- this act was committed, it was the OVR Cair that is responsible and; according to my information, they undertook everything that was under their duty, which means that they informed the public prosecutor's office and the investigating judge.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will kindly ask you now to look at the document in tab 93 from this same binder.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is Exhibit P261.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: It is an Official Note from the OVR Cair, submitted by Blagoja Toskovski; Official Note number 537.

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, is this the information that you received with regards to that -- one of the detained individuals?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this should be it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will kindly ask you now to look at the document after tab 94.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is Exhibit P46.16, under seal.

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see the document. In this case --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, please tell us. This is what I wanted to ask you: What is this?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a document which is submitted to the basic public prosecutor's office in Skopje by the OVR Cair. This act supplements the criminal report; that is to say, it means that the necessary expertise was sent to the public prosecutor's office on fire-arm residue as well as an Official Note, I believe the one we saw previously. This is the report on this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Where do you see that this document was filed with the basic public prosecutor's office?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the title, it states it is prepared by OVR Cair; and immediately following, it states "to" and the abbreviation "OJO," which means public prosecutor's office.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You stated that the Official Note number 537 was attached to this, as it says in the text, information on a person who has died and that was actually the Official Note that we had seen a while ago. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you please now go look at the document in tab 93. So that is the Official Note that was submitted to the prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, is this the legally prescribed way in which the police informs the prosecutor of the fact that an individual has died?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is within the framework of procedures.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You stated that after filing such report, your obligation is to undertake certain actions only upon a request of the judge or the prosecutor; have I understood you well.

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. From the moment that the public prosecutor and especially the investigating judge becomes involved, then we are, so to say, under their command and we are obliged to carry out their requests or orders.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could the public prosecutor, on the investigating judge's request, obtain certain data from other organs?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the right of the investigating judge and his assessment who he or she might involve in the work, and from whom documents will be requested or measures will be required.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could the police -- or rather, does the police have the right or the duty to tell the judge whom to request data from?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let's look now at the document after tab 124, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is Exhibit P54.052, under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is a document from the investigative department of the Basic Court Skopje II. Can you tell us to whom was this memo addressed by the investigating judge and who was requested to provide some data?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The investigating judge submitted this document to the general city hospital, Skopje, and requested the data he deemed necessary.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will draw your attention to the paragraph that starts with the words: "The accused, Bajrami, Nevaip; Ramadani; Ismail; et cetera..." Do you see this paragraph?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: It reads here: "The accused, Bajrami, Nevaip; Ramadani, Ismail; Qaili, Atulla; Ametovski, Adem, immediately after the events of 12th, August, 2001, in the area of Ljuboten village, Skopje region, were transferred and kept at the general city hospital, Skopje, because of their injuries; while the accused, Qaili, Atulla, had passed away as we were informed by the police station Cair. "Considering that this is a detention case, there is a need to immediately inform us about the health status of the accused, Bajrami Nevaip; Ramadani, Ismail; and Adem Ametovksi: What injuries they sustained, are they able to communicate with the court, and are the bodies ... [as interpreted]. "Considering that pursuant to the Law on Criminal Procedure, it is necessary that they are questioned by an investigating judge." Mr. Stojanovski, is it clear from this document that the OVR Cair informed the investigating judge of the death of Atulla Qaili?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: From this correspondence, tell me, is it clear that the investigating judge decided to request the data from the general city hospital, information regarding the injuries of other persons that were at the hospital as he was informed?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, according to this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Does this document corroborate your testimony that the investigating judge is the body that decides what are data to be requested and from which bodies?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said previously, this is the exclusive right of the investigating judge.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you please look now at the document after tab 125.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is Exhibit P54.027, under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This, too, is a document from the investigating department of the Basic Court Skopje. The investigating judge signed is Velce Pancevski. It is addressed to the Skopje prison in Skopje, and it should be received by the director. In this note, the third paragraph reads: "After the conversation with Dr. Nikola Gruev, director of Skopje City General Hospital, the investigating judge was informed that the condition of detainees, Bajrami Nevaip and Ramadani Ismail, has improved and that they should be re-examined in a few days," et cetera. Does this document corroborate again, Mr. Stojanovski, that it is the investigating judge who decides which organ is to be informed and that the investigating judge was already in communication with the director of the city General Hospital with regards to the injuries of some individuals?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does confirm it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will kindly ask you now to look at the document after tab 126.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is it Exhibit P54.028, under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is, again, a document, signed by the investigating judge of the Basic Court Skopje II, sent to the penitentiary institution, prison, Skopje. And if we look at the second paragraph, the judge says: "In order to establish the identity of the detainee, Qaili Atulla, son of Avdi, father, and Hava, mother, born on 3rd of November 1965 in Skopje, resident of village of Ljuboten, Skopje," and then there is the ID number, "primary school education, Albanian, national of the Republic of Macedonia, the investigating judge sent a letter, KI number 436/01, of 16th of August, 2001, to the Forensic Medicine Institutes and to the Ministry of Interior of the Republic of Macedonia, OVR Skopje, in order to obtain data on the detainee from the registry of deceased." Mr. Stojanovski, does this also corroborate the notion that it was the investigating judge who decided and who was actually the only individual able to request the data from the Forensic Medicine Institute?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you please look at the document in tab 127.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is Exhibit P54.029, under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is a document sent by the court to the city administration of internal affairs. So this is the body where you work, but to the sector for internal affairs, to the registry department. Does this document corroborate your evidence that it is the investigating judge who decides which data are requested from the police and when the police has a duty to respond?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, my anxiety level is rising. We've heard a series of leading questions. I realise my colleague is doing this, in part, at least, to save some time. However, several of these questions are touching on points that are actually quite crucial to the case, and perhaps she could try to phrase some of her questions in a less leading way.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I asked all the questions already of the witness. I'm just showing the documents. He previously already answered each and every of these questions. So if you believe that this is not the proper way for me to carry out my direct examination, I will follow your instructions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The objection is made that you are leading. It is the case. You are also being very repetitive. In the course of the evidence of this witness last week and now, we have gone over some of these things three times at least. So I think you can, A, avoid leading; and, B, watch what has already been dealt with a little more carefully. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I will just mention that the documents in tabs 128 and 129, which are Exhibits P54.030 and P52.12, are documents that have the same nature as the ones that I asked the witness about.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: In line 8:4, it is not "OVR Skopje," it is the "head office of the Ministry of Interior."

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will kindly ask you now, Mr. Stojanovski, to look at the document in tab 135.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is Exhibit P28, under seal. In addition to the documents that I indicated were of same nature, I would also like to include the document -- the Exhibit P120 in tab 130; the Exhibit P46.4 in tab 131; and the exhibit in tab 132, that is Exhibit P54.059.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now, Mr. Stojanovski, to look at this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is Exhibit P28, under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is a document produced by the OVR Cair. Would you tell me what is it?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a special report, a supplement to the criminal report that was drafted by OVR Cair, which, due to the problems in the course of drafting and lack of time, was filed without the expertise of fire-arms and without photographs of these weapons. In cases such as these, OVR Cair is obliged to supplement this report with the evidence which were secured in the course of their work.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And just for the transcript, with regards to this answer, we have the Exhibit P47.22.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you please now look at the document in tab 137.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is Exhibit P52.13, under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is a document signed by three investigating judges, sent -- would you tell us to whom is this document addressed?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I believe that we mentioned already that the OVR Cair has produced three criminal reports, and the investigating judges responsible for these cases have filed the request with the department for internal affairs, OVR Cair, by which they request additional data on the information that took place in the period between the 10th and the 12th of August in the area of village Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In connection with this response, I refer you to P50.009 [as interpreted], under seal, and Exhibit P50.20 [as interpreted], under seal. They are behind tabs 138 and 139. "P50.29," I believe I stated that. "50.010" is what line 20 should state.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you please be so kind as to look at the document behind tab 139, which is Exhibit P50.010, and tell me whether you're familiar with this report and in connection with what?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a report produced upon a request of the SVR Skopje; namely, as I said previously during this evidence, a committee was established by the Minister Boskoski to investigate the events in the village of Ljuboten. I was appointed contact person for cooperation with that committee. So upon a request of the committee the department of internal affairs, OVR Cair produced this information.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. On Friday, you stated that after an attempted on-site investigation, the burial of the persons who died took place. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you said that after that, there was no point in going to the scene of crime because there was no scene of crime any longer. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, what is required to enable you to answer the basic questions as to how and as a result what the persons died, after these same individuals had been buried?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Considering what was taking place there, the only way to ascertain those things that you mentioned as needed was through exhumation and post-mortem; so if we wanted to establish the cause of death, that is.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Who was the only individual authorised to authorise the exhumation and autopsy; do you know?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pursuant to our legislation, the public prosecutor is the only organ that can file such motion with the investigating judge, and the investigating judge is the only organ that can approve and enforce that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know if a request for exhumation and autopsy was filed; and if so, by whom and on whose initiative?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no such proposal at that time, as far as I know. But I know that later there was certain initiative on the part of the ministry to undertake such activities.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me state for the record, Exhibits 1D33; then P55.02, under seal; Exhibit 1D46; and Exhibit 1D70 -- 73, rather, 1D73.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please look at document behind tab 146, which is 1D47.

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat this?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tab 146, which is Exhibit 1D47.

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's all right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think we have that document, 1D47. N001-0 - or rather, pages 1D1949 in Macedonian and 1950 -- or rather, 1D001950 [as interpreted] is the page in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski, this is a letter from the investigating judge to the head of the public security bureau in connection with the need to find some information concerning exhumations. Please, tell me, were you aware of this document?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that OVR Cair was tasked with carrying out certain verifications and then responding to the investigating judge.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If the director, Mitevski, in fact, received this document, would he be the authorised individual to double-check the reliability of the information contained therein, or would he have some other duties?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The route to follow is the following: The director forwards this document to the sector for internal affairs, Skopje; and from there, we forward it to the department of internal affairs, OVR Cair, so that they process it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Look at document behind tab 147, which is 1D190. Can you tell me whose document this is, and what the report therein refers to?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a document produced by the OVR Cair, and it deals with the request that they received from the investigating judge; and through this document, they inform him of the outcome of the verifications or double-checks that they carried out.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In connection with this answer, I refer you to Exhibit P104 and 1D189.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, what is your knowledge about the OVR Cair, in fact, receiving the information the investigating judge sought or not?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, the OVR Cair did not succeed in fully following the request of the investigating judge.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, do you have any information as to why the OVR Cair failed to obtain the information?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Primarily because the population of Ljuboten village did not want to cooperate with the police at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Since you knew that the residents were not forthcoming in their cooperation, did you personally, since you worked in the crime police department in Skopje, try to assist OVR Cair in obtaining some information at least?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maintaining contact with the international organisations was within the remits of my duty, so I had contacts with the security office of the United Nations, OSCE, representatives of foreign embassies, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Some of the individuals from these organisations and bodies that were present in Skopje, did you, in addition to having business relations with them, have social relations with them?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Considering that we had frequent -- yes, we built -- you might say that we had social relations as well, friendly relations.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you name some of the individuals you had good business relations but with whom you were also on friendly terms?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We cooperated with the OSCE the most and with the security office of the United Nations in Skopje. The closest contacts and the friendliest contacts we had at the OSCE were with Mr. Henry Bolton; and with regards to the United Nations office, I believe that Mr. Tom was there at the time, and then Ms. Julie.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Had you ever pointed to the problem in obtaining information to these international associates, and did you ever seek assistance from them?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in particular, from the OSCE, considering that they had access to the village and considering their contacts with the population, with the inhabitants there; however, they pursued their policy, of course. So they kept us in isolation to an extent. And with regards to the access to the village, entering the village, their position was that it was too early and that priority is the restoration of confidence in the population.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski, do you know if at some point the international community got involved in the process of exhumation in the village of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but that was later. That was in the following year.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were you involved in the process of exhumation as the police force at that point in time?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The SVR Skopje was not involved; however, the police forensics of the MOI were involved, yes. They were the only body that was involved.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before starting the process of exhumation, should there -- should some preliminary actions precede that process, do you know, or could these have been done only by the police force in Macedonia, or the judiciary?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I mentioned that the investigating judge had sent previously a request to obtain certain information. However, if we speak specifically about the exhumation, then probably we would need to know the identity of the persons. And considering the time that had lapsed, we needed to secure certain information that would aid the identification of the bodies and, of course, the location where they were buried. However, the OVR Cair, the department for internal affairs, Cair, was not able to secure such information.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In reference to this answer, I refer you to P55.09, P49.033, P49.034, P55.10, P55.55, P55.28, P55.27, P55.21, P55.25, P49.014. All these documents are under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski, did you ever receive the results or the findings from the exhumations and the autopsies of the bodies exhumed?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not have any opportunity to see that, and we have no access to such type of documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I refer you to Exhibits P46.15; P45.19 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: P55.19.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] P55.34; Exhibit P49.003; P49.004; P55.20.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, a moment ago you said that as the police, you were not involved in assisting the court in the process of exhumations and autopsies. What was your view or your assessment of the situation at the time? How did it sit with you? How did you take it.

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can give you only my personal feeling about that. That was, in my opinion, removing the sovereignty, in a way, of the state. And if, when the events at Aracinovo took place, I started to doubt, I believe that these events confirmed the notion that Macedonia became a state where the -- instead of rule of law, the political rules were prevailing. So the politics took precedence over the enforcement of the law, which means that someone prohibited us from performing our duties that we were charged with.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, Please, Mr. Stojanovski, was the subject of your interest only the events that transpired in the village, or also the events that took place in the aftermath of that incident at check-points and police stations?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: That's another leading question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I rephrase the question or should I move on to another question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Try rephrasing, Ms. Residovic, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski, in addition to exhibiting interest in what had happened in the victim, did the police show interest in any other events?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: During that time, the media published speculations that civilians were killed in the village, that the police had ill-treated the residents of the village at the check-points, and that the police ill-treated the detainees, individuals who were brought in with regards to this event. When we received those information, we had the duty to check it because the reputation of the police was at stake. I can say that, on the basis of all the actions, measures that were taken, and in which I myself participated directly, we were not able to verify or otherwise that information. At the same time, there was a lot of pressure on the Ministry of Interior to examine that information, and if they proved accurate to detective the perpetrators.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski, you already stated that the Albanian population from the village refused to cooperate with the police. Did anyone report any sort of mistreatment carried out at the hands of the police, the police station, or the OVR or SVR?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Considering that the committee had already been established and I was appointed a contact person, I also processed some requests that came from the committee. I, myself, interviewed all heads of the departments for internal affairs where persons were brought in, in relation to the Ljuboten events, and not one of them confirmed that such things had taken place. There was no complaint. There was not a single complaint or petition filed with regard to the detention. No breach of duty was registered. Simply, without cooperation, the cooperation with the residents or with the allegedly ill-treated, it was not possible to secure anything of the sort. Although, you know, pursuant to our rules, such complaint or report could be filed over the telephone. It was not necessary for anyone to come to the police station to report such incident, but nothing of the sort was available.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did at any point the prosecutor, the court, or the defence council representing the individual against whom the proceedings were initiated, inform you that those individuals had complained to them of the police having overstepped their duty, mistreated them, or in any abused them at the police station or elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think, in the previous answer, we clarified the position of the police and that of the public prosecutor or investigating judge. Once the persons were handed over to the investigating judge, and once they were brought in --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. We have already heard that. Did they let you know that they had been told in turn by someone that someone had complained to them about the conduct of the police?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not receive such information.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: A moment ago, you said that the VMRO [as interpreted] had also insisted on the matters being sorted out. Can you tell me who were in touch with at the VMRO [as interpreted] in contention with the clearing up or sorting out of the situation in connection with Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how many persons went through my office in regards to this event, all of them requesting information, requesting that checks be made. I could mention some of them because there's no way that I could remember all of these persons. First of all, this is the crime police at the MOI. I think Mr. Mihajlovski was assistant there at the time. Ms. Katica Jovanovska, who I think came to my office every other day, went directly to OVR Cair to conduct her checks. Then she was replaced by Ms. Galevska [as interpreted]. There was a working group for investigating war crimes. I did not have so much contact with them. Our duties were to provide them with logistical and staff support. I also had contacts with representatives from international organisations. However, I will say again this information was not confirmed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski, you are now testifying before the Trial Chamber. Tell me, under the circumstances in which you tried to clear the situation up concerning Ljuboten, what is your opinion? Were you able to do anything more than what you did to obtain other and different information?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: One can always do better. However, having in mind the circumstances in which we were working, I think I explained that my colleagues did not go home for days, that they were moving targets at that period. Although, I can say that there's always room to do more and to do better, I am personally am satisfied by what they did. Even under such circumstances, they carried out their legal duties. One could not ask for more.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski, let me ask you this at the end: If someone were to claim before this Chamber that you had issued an order to the chief of Cair, to issue with a vehicle some persons who is arrived Cair, to issue them with weapons although this was contrary to his wishes, to go to the meeting of the battalion of the 1st Guards Brigade, that you were an eye-witness of the police mistreating the individuals who were brought there, and that, as a result of that, you were duty-bound to launch an inquiry into this, what would you, Mr. Stojanovski, respond to such an assertion?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mentioned several things. All single one of them are lies.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski, why do you think that someone would not be telling the truth before this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: How can the witness answer that, Ms. Residovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I put the question, and I'll withdraw it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And this will complete my examination of the witness. Thank you, Mr. Stojanovski, for answering my questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Residovic. Mr. Apostolski, is there any questions you have for this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. I will have several questions for this witness, and I think that my questioning would take about 15 to 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That may be a very good timing, Mr. Apostolski, and we'll have a break after your questions. Thank you. Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wanted to inform the Court of this, so we can plan our time.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Witness Petre Stojanovski. My name is Antonio Apostolski, and I'm the Defence attorney for Johan Tarculovski. My colleague, Edina Residovic, alerted you of the fact that you understand her language. You understand the language which I speak even better since we are communicating with the Macedonian language. However, you will have to wait for the questions to be interpreted so that the Trial Chamber can better follow the questioning. Did you understand?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You said that the detainees from Ljuboten of 12th of August, 2001 were given a paraffin glove test. Did you recall testifying to this?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This was the procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you tell us what was the aim of the paraffin glove test?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Usually, these kinds of tests are requested when there is suspicion that the persons used fire-arms.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that the positive result of the paraffin glove test sets grounds for suspicion that a certain person has used armed weapons?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In accordance to my knowledge, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it true that the positive results of the paraffin glove test is the basis for filing a criminal report to the basic public prosecutor's office against a person; that is to say, that that person has used a fire-arm?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think previously we saw some such criminal reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You also said that, during the operation of the Macedonian security forces of 12th of August, 2001, weapons were seized from the detained persons. Do you recall this?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This was in the case of the persons who were detained in the police station Mirkovci.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that the terrorist organisation NLA had to be disarmed with the Essential Harvest Operation in September 2001?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that part of the terrorist group NLA did not give back or return the weapons? Do you have knowledge to this extent?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is such knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that after 2001 the Macedonian police carried out several actions, whereby bunkers were detected, bunkers of concealed weapons used by the terrorist group NLA?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What's the relevance of that question? This case deals with the events of 2001, particularly the events in August 2001.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm aware of this event prior to asking the question; however, my ensuing questions might also include the period after 2001. But my questions will be very concrete about the events around the village of Ljuboten; therefore, my ensuing questions about focus on the village of Ljuboten. This was the basis for putting forth my ensuing questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Are you asking about bunkers in Ljuboten or in the vicinity of Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. This would be my following question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Your first question isn't limited in that way, you see. I'm not quite sure what you were directing that question to.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My questioning about bunkers of weapons on the territory of the -- in and around Ljuboten, after 2001, is asked because the case of the Defence is that in the village of Ljuboten, before 2001 and after 2001, as well as in the course of 2001, groupations [as interpreted] of the terrorist group NLA were active, whereby Ljuboten was used for was used for hiding weapons as well as for logistics for the terrorist group NLA, as well as to other previous terrorist groups that were active on the territory of the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the issue in this case is whether -- let me correct myself. One of the issues in this case is whether there were members of the National Liberation Army in and around Ljuboten on the 12th of August, 2001. The Prosecution does not see how the fact that a bunker may have existed in or around Ljuboten after 2001, and I don't know how many years after Mr. Apostolski is going to be asking about, can be relevant to the core issue of this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Saxon, there are number of potential issues. One is whether there were NLA terrorists in Ljuboten at the time we're concerned with in August of 2001; whether, even if there were no terrorists there, security forces had some reasonable basis for belief that there were such terrorists. There is also the question of whether there was a state of armed conflict in August, and whether it had existed before and perhaps whether it had continued later. So I don't think we can narrow the issues as narrowly as you were putting them, and I'm sure there could be more. Nor is it immediately apparent that what happened after 2001 is going to help us in this case very much. Mr. Apostolski, I think the problem with your question that prompted all this is that it was completely unlimited in time and location. You just said: Were there bunkers find anywhere in Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, my questions will be focussed on the territory around Ljuboten, and it will be followed by two documents which I wish to put before the witness. With your permission, I would like to continue my questioning in this line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, if you can put your questions on that confined factual basis, yes, Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness please be shown document 65 ter 2D00502.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Witness, in the screen before you, do you see on the left-hand side the document title, which it states: "Republic of Macedonia, Ministry of Interior, Skopje sector of the UBK, Skopje"?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you see that it was prepared on the 25th of March, 2004?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Underneath, nature of the material: "Report from an interview with the operational position Silo." The interview took place on 24 March 2004.

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you tell us what kind of document this is?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an information regarding terrorism and extremism; that is to say, activities of the NLA in the village of Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you tell us who drafted this document?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This document was drafted by the sector of the security and counter-intelligence bureau of Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I would read parts of this document to you: "This is an interview with the operational position Silo, who, through direct contacts with persons, took part in the deployment of weapons stationed in the village of Ljuboten, given by the so-called NLA for the defence of the village of Ljuboten, whereby the only responsible person was Alimi Baki, so-called Commander Lisi, a history teacher at the primary school in the village of Ljuboten, whereby weapons were collected from several points which were foreseen for the defence of the village of Ljuboten. "And it is emphasised that there were two Gulinovs. So heavy machine-guns were collected, one with ammunition and the other slightly damaged and without ammunition; three large light machine-guns with stands; a large quantity of automatic rifles, some of them so-called Tulumbashi. According to the information given by the source, over 150 pieces, ammunition, hand-grenades, and various so-called Zoljas hand-held rocket launchers."

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see the second page of this document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: "A small number of anti-personnel mines, as well as several anti-tank mines. (At the moment, the person, Sherafedim Bajrami, also known as Shef, is in possession of one such mine and plans to lay it on the road used by the Ministry of Interior and Macedonian army patrols, the only reason being to avenge the death of his two brothers killed in the operation during the military conflict in Ljuboten)." Does this part of the report of this interview correspond to your knowledge that part of the terrorist group NLA did not return the weapons after the essential harvest operation?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Apostolski, this appears to be a report of information received in 2004, is that correct, and it's information received from a person who is not identified in this report? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. On the basis of this interview, the Macedonian police carried out an action later on, which is the next document I want to show to the witness, whereby arms was detected and seized from the village of Ljuboten. Therefore, this document is just the basis for showing the other document to the witness and so finish my line of questioning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is it the intention of your Defence case to call this informant as a witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honours, it is not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Your basis for seeing this as relevant is what was found in 2004, is that what you're saying, by a police search?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. On the basis of this information, after several months, weapons were found in the village of Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And it pertains to the events of 2001, because these are weapons which were hidden in 2001.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Just a point of clarification, Your Honour. The Prosecution believes that nowhere in this document does it refer to weapons located or deposited in Ljuboten during 2001. The document is completely unclear. These weapons could have been deposited in Ljuboten, if they were, in 2003 or 2004, 2002. The document simply doesn't say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: In fact, there could be implications from the document that these weapons were collected, to enable an individual to make some response in respect of some of the deaths that occurred in Ljuboten with which we are concerned. The implementation of that being that the weapons could have been collected later rather than before the relevant events in Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Apostolski, the Chamber takes the view that this information has no sufficient connection that has been demonstrated with any event that we're concerned with in 2001. All sorts of weapons might be found in 2004 or 2008, even, in a place. We need to know whether there were weapons in 2001, and anything you seem to be intending to adduce does not go to establish that. So you should not pursue this line of questioning, unless you've got some way to demonstrate that these weapons were there in 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I was aware even prior to asking those questions about the problem which could arise. But I felt that this information, as well as the information that weapons were found in Ljuboten after the events which are not relevant to this case, I would like to point out that after the events in that same village, weapons were found in a concrete place in a concrete house. Therefore, I felt that it would assist the Trial Chamber in establishing the factual state of affairs. However, if the Chamber believes that there is no grounds to pursue this, then I will not show the next document and I will end my line of questioning here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That is the position of the Chamber. Thank you, Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. I think that is a convenient time, then, for the first break, or the break, and we resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, during the recess, I spoke to my colleague, the Prosecutor, and he would not object the proposal I'm making. I'm tendering the documents that I showed to the witness as exhibits, and I'm referring to the following documents and I kindly ask the Chamber to receive them in evidence. The first one is 65 ter 1D1238. That was in tab 10, and this is an order --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Just pause there while the registry officer catches up to that. That will be received as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document will become Exhibit 1D291, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next document is 65 ter 406. It was in tab 43.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D292, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 65 ter 1D1219, which was in tab 173. Those are criminal reports filed against certain individuals, because of violence against Albanian property in Skopje.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 65 ter 1D --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document will be received as Exhibit 1D293, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the next two documents are also criminal reports. These are 65 ter 1D1220 and 65 ter 1D1221. They were in tabs 174 and 175.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter 1D1220 will become Exhibit 1D294; and 65 ter 1D1221 will become Exhibit 1D295, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And, at the end, 65 ter 1170. The document was in tab 113. That is a document coming from the analytics department of the OVR Cair.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be received as Exhibit 1D296, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Stojanovski. My name is Dan Saxon. I'm from originally the city of Boston in the United States, and I represent the Prosecutor in this case and I've got some questions for you this morning. First of all, is it correct that you understand and you can read a fair amount of the English language?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: One could say this, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And do you have any kind of a family relationship with Ljube Boskoski?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Was Mr. Boskoski the godfather or "kum" to you or to someone close to you?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours, you won't be surprised that the Prosecution has prepared a couple of binders of materials that we'd like to use with this witness, and we'd like to distribute the first binder now. I'm grateful to our usher for her literally doing the heavy lifting.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, Mr. Stojanovski, perhaps, with the usher's assistance, you could turn to what is tab 2 in that binder that's in front of you, and if you could turn to the Macedonian version, Mr. Stojanovski.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This is 65 ter 1146, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And you'll see, Mr. Stojanovski, that this is actually a copy of the -- of your personnel file from the Ministry of Interior. Do you see that on the first page?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if we can go to -- if you go to around the third or fourth page, you will see what appears to be your resume or a history of your employment with the ministry. Can you keep going, please to the page that looks like this. Page looks like this, Mr. Stojanovski.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It has ERN number N006-7979.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if we can just take a look, please, at this report of your employment in the Ministry of Interior, maybe we could start by focussing on the year 1996. You see there is an entry that, by November 1996, you were the temporary head of the department for illegal trade in the crime police. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, for example, in that position, when you were the head of that department, who were your subordinates? Who did you supervise?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, the department for illegal trade worked on matters related to illegal trade of arms and narcotic. Within this framework, my subordinates were the heads of those units.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And when you say "the heads of those units," you're referring to heads of those units within the Republic headquarters of the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the crime police of the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And that would include, of course, the heads of the units for illegal trade in the different SVRs, right?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The line goes through the heads of the SVRs.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Then through the heads of the SVRs, you could task the heads of the unit for illegal trade within a SVR, couldn't you?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Depending on the situation. If we're working on a joint case, then I could.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And you could also task, depending on the situation, the head or the heads of the units for illegal trade within OVRs, couldn't you?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are no such units at the OVRs.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. So at least, though, you could provide instructions to the units for illegal trade in the SVRs, right?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we're working on matters such as these, and when we believe that instructions have to be given to the units for illegal trade at the SVR, we draft the instruction. We prepare the instruction, but it has to be approved also by the head of the crime police, depending on the type of instructions, also by the director for public security.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And once it's approved by the head of the crime police, and the director for public security if necessary, then the instruction would go down the chain to the SVR, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It goes to the SVR and in the unit for illegal trade at the SVR.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, if necessary, if some work had to be done, then, at an OVR, the appropriate orders would also be issued to the appropriate head of the OVR. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is a task for the SVR, for the head of the unit for illegal trade at the SVR, which organises and establishes cooperation with the unit of internal affairs --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I see --

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- with the OVR.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. So, then if the head of --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the Prosecutor, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. So if the head of the unit for illegal trade at the SVR needs the cooperation of an individual or colleagues in a OVR, what does that person do, or what would that person do back in 2001?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Coordination within the SVR goes through the head of the SVR. This means that if there is a need for undertaking certain measures, the coordination of these units is conducted by the sector for internal affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And the instruction to undertake certain measures within an OVR would come from whom at that time?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, the coordination is part of the work of the head of the SVR Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So put another way, then, if the -- if additional measures or tasks are needed to be performed, then it would be the head of the SVR Skopje who would issue instructions to the head of the particular OVR to make sure those tasks were performed. Correct?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: One could say that, yes. The coordination is carried out by the head of the sector for internal affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And, again, going back to the late 1990s when you were the head of the directorate for illegal trade at the crime police, who were your superiors then? Or maybe an easier question: Who was your immediate superior at that time, say, back in 1997?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were several while I was at the crime police: Mr. Trenevski, Mr. Zafirovski.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What were their positions?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Heads of the crime police at the MOI.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: At the Republic level?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if you're -- if those superiors felt that a particular measure or task had to be undertaken, they might issue an instruction to you which you might forward to an SVR. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In essence, initiatives went the other way around, because the heads of the crime police are experienced, but this doesn't mean that they're skilled in all areas. If one of the specialised departments establishes the need for an instruction, then it initiates this through or at the head of the crime police.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And when the head of the crime police would then approve the initiative and would issue that instruction, that was needed, right?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, if it agreed with the facts, proposals, and understandings that we gave. Nonetheless --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nonetheless, for certain issues and matters, only the director could approve a certain instruction and that it be sent to the territorial organisational units.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. So if I understand you correctly, at least in the late 1990s and up until 2001, first of all, the head of the crime police, if that person agreed with the proposal, that person would issue an instruction down the chain through you, perhaps, for the appropriate to be carried out, right? That's one way something would occur?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In principle. In concrete cases, then it's the head of the crime police. If these are general tasks that encompass other sectors for internal affairs, then it should be the director for public security.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And when the director for public security approved of a particular task or initiative, then the director for public security would issue that instruction or issue that approval, and his instruction would then pass down the chain of command to the relevant operative person, is that right, in those particular situations?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We prepared the material, and we submitted for approval. The material which is approved, and there were also cases when it was not approved, is returned to us. If approved, we distributed further.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if these particular initiatives were not approved, then those measures would not be carried out. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If our proposal is not accepted, then it is not carried out.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And that was the situation in 2001, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And when those -- for example, if approval for a particular initiative was given and then the measure was carried out, the particular unit or colleague at the ministry would then send a report to their superiors about the measures that they undertook, wouldn't they?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, to the sector -- to the head of the sector for internal affairs and to the head of the relevant directorate at the crime police.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: When you say "the head of the relevant directorate at the crime place," you're referring to the relevant directorate at the crime police at the Republic level, right?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: To simplify, if it is a narcotic case or instructions about a narcotics issue, then the measures, as per the received instruction, should be reported to the SVR where their work where the colleagues work and then to the head of the directorate. If were more simply to say it this way, it would be sent to me, if we're talking about the time when I was at that position.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, at that time, when you were in that position back in the late 1990s, your position was at the headquarters of the ministry for the republic level, wasn't it, at the national level.

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The crime police was part of Bureau for Public Security; therefore, one could say at the level of the republic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Then we see, from the history of your career, that since the mid-1990s, you began to hold a series of positions of responsibility. In 1998, you were the head of the sector for illegal weapons trafficking, the crime police; and then in 2000, you became the deputy for crime police matters at the cabinet of the SVR Skopje; and then in 2001, if I'm reading this correctly, you became an assistant head at the crime police for SVR Skopje in the beginning of August. Is that about right?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And you also told us earlier that, after 1995, you attended several courses and seminars related to illegal drug trafficking, and also you attended several management courses, right?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You attended courses in Paris, in Germany, in Bulgaria, and within Macedonia, itself, at the faculty for security. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And it's true, isn't it, that within the Ministry of Interior, to be selected to attend courses abroad is considered an important professional honour and distinction, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not understand your question. The goal of the training is to train people, not to award distinctions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I understand what the goals of training is. But, for example, the ministry would not send just any police officer to a training course in Paris, would they? They would send people who have performed their duties with particular competence and distinction, isn't it, and dedication?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When a need is established for special or supplemental education, additional education, the SVRs propose and nominate colleagues which they believe require such training and whom they believe will have a serious approach towards such training. This proposal is most often then verified by the crime police and the director approved it, if this was the case of training courses abroad.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And it would be true, wouldn't it, that you were selected to go to these courses abroad because you were known as an officer who took a serious approach? Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are two alternatives, two options. Someone felt that I needed additional training and that someone felt that I would show and demonstrate a serious approach towards such training.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I certainly respect your modesty, Mr. Stojanovski, but I'll put the question a different way: You did take a serious approach to your work and to your training, didn't you, throughout your career?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would hope so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, in fact, in the late 1990s, you were awarded several bonuses, if that's the right word, for your particular efforts in solving certain cases, such as discovering narcotics, confiscating explosives. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that, yes, I was relatively successful.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If you could turn, please, to what is the -- it should be the sixth page in your language. Maybe it's one page further on. No, I'm sorry. I'm sorry, Mr. Stojanovski. Not tab 6. But in the same series of documents, it's a document that looks like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Maybe the usher could assistant. It has ERN number N006-7978.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If you're with me, Mr. Stojanovski, this is a document dated the 5th of June, 2001. It's addressed to the sector of legal and personnel matters of the Ministry of Interior of the Republic of Macedonia. It's the -- the subject is the award of a financial reward, and it is a proposal to award you an award of 15.000 dinars. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And it says that: "During 2001, the named person manifested particular professionalism, efficiency, and creativity in performing the established plans and programmes in the area of work and organisation of the crime police at SVR Skopje." Are you following me?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Then the next paragraph talks about your "contributions to detecting and disclosing a large number of criminal acts, as well as capturing and arresting the perpetrators." Then, in the next paragraph, it mentions you and talks about your demonstrated initiatives and the contributions that you made to the results of the crime police at SVR Skopje. Then the proposal is signed by the head of the sector, Zoran Efremov. Mr. Efremov, he was your boss at the time, wasn't he? Am I right?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is so.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If you could cast your modesty aside for a moment, tell us why you were normal indicated for this award. What were these achievements and accomplishments that you -- that you accomplished during the first part of 2001?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The crime police of SVR Skopje, that is to say, the units which I was directly superior to, successfully carried out their tasks, under conditions elaborated on -- on several occasions previously; and this act, in itself, working under such conditions, presumed a solid organisation within and efforts which exceeded the usual work tasks. Also, at that period, our manner of work was through daily meetings with my subordinates where we looked into problems and we sought common solutions. I believe that I succeeded with some initiatives in directing my colleagues to carry out their work tasks as successfully as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And so, just so that I understand you, you've described the extraordinarily complex and difficult circumstances in which you and your colleagues were working in 2001, and at least part of the reason why you were nominated for this award is because, in spite of those difficulties, you and your colleagues persevered and you managed to accomplish your tasks. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Generally speaking, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if you turn to the next page, we see that this proposal was being submitted to crime police department.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This is ERN N006-7986.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It's dated the 11th of June, 2001. Then if you turn to the page once more, Mr. Stojanovski, you'll see a decision. And if you're having trouble finding it, maybe the usher can assist. It has ERN N006-7977.

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is not on the following. This is on the previous page, as far as I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Then it's my fault. The important thing is that you see it.

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. So, we see here, this decision dated the 15th of June, 2001, and this is decision signed by Ljube Boskoski, the minister at that point. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And this decision, effectively it approves the proposal to give you a financial reward, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The minister endorsed the opinion of my direct superior and accepted his opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And that's because, according to the Law on Internal Affairs, decisions on awards -- final decisions are to be made by the minister. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I should read the law to be able to answer this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Actually, I may be citing to you the wrong law, so I'm going to come back to this point later on. This was the decision that awarded you this award. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, pursuant to the law and the collective agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if you can turn to what is ERN N006-7973, this is a decision dated the 24th of July, 2001. You'll see it's signed by the Minister of the Interior then, Ljube Boskoski, and it's a decision redeploying you. Do you see that, Mr. Stojanovski?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And you're being redeployed as the assistant head officer for the crime police in the SVR Skopje as of 1st of August, 2001. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a decision appointing me, but I occupied that post before even, so this just confirms it. Since when I became assistant head of the police for the SVR Skopje, it took place during the time when Mr. Dosta Dimovska was the Minister of the Interior, while this decision is just a technical correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So, now, Dosta Dimovska, he stepped down as Minister of the Interior in May of 2001, right?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, before that time, you were already performing the functions of this particular position, assistant head officer for crime police in the SVR Skopje. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. First of all, the title of my post was deputy to the head of the SVR Skopje; and from 1st of August, 2001, it is assistant to the head for crime police. The level in the hierarchy remained unchanged.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. But I'm just trying to clarify something that you told us earlier. If the translation is correct, you explained to us that you had occupied this position even before this document was issued on the 24th of July, 2001, and I'm just trying to clarify what you mean by that. Does that mean you were performing the functions of the position that's named in this document prior to July 2001?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. So, there were no changes with regards to the duties that I was to perform, except that the title "deputy" was changed into "assistant."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. So, de facto, you were performing the same duties prior to the date that this decision was issued, right?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. But with regards to the change of the systemization, titles in the post of the SVR Skopje, the title of my post was changed as well; and because of that change, a new decision was issued.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I see. Okay. All right. And, hopefully, the next document, the very next page in your binder, hopefully, will be another decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This has ERN number N006-7975, dated the 3rd of October, 2002.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And this document is a decision, because of particular engagement in accomplishing the function of the Ministry of Interior, you are being awarded a pistol, an HS-2000 9-millimetre pistol; and this decision is signed by Ljube Boskoski. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The proposal of my superior at that time, Mr. Kocovski, was endorsed and accepted by Mr. Boskoski.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
